title: 拉沙德·罗宾逊：与扎克伯格交锋，我学到了“对话”与“谈判”的区别
speaker: Rashad Robinson

segments.en: How did you think about the dynamic that you had and representing people who had real grievances and wanted real change with folks who'd really reached the session on where they hadn't been thinking about that very much?
segments.zh: 你如何看待这种动态：你代表有真实不满、想要真正改变的人们，与那些已经达到一定地位、却不太考虑这些的人打交道？

segments.en: So I tell a lot of stories in the book about this because I think it's really important to unlock for folks what happens behind the scenes because some of these lessons of going in and trying to push Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg at Facebook to do something different.
segments.zh: 我在书中讲了很多这样的故事，因为我认为让人们了解幕后发生的事情非常重要。这些教训包括走进Facebook，试图推动马克·扎克伯格和谢丽尔·桑德伯格做出改变。

segments.en: What you were doing is yes and getting and getting change is actually similar to like going into your school board meeting or going into your local library board or whatever.
segments.zh: 你所做的，以及获得改变，实际上类似于参加学校董事会会议或当地图书馆董事会会议等。

segments.en: And you know one of the things I learned in those back and forth.
segments.zh: 在这些来回交锋中，我学到的一件事是……

segments.en: Well first of all my first meeting where we finally built up enough leverage to go and meet with Mark and Sheryl after there was a lot of back and forth in the media and they had hired a PR firm to attack me in the organization.
segments.zh: 首先，我的第一次会议，我们终于建立了足够的杠杆去与马克和谢丽尔会面，此前媒体上有很多来回，他们还雇了公关公司攻击我和我的组织。

segments.en: I get to Menlo Park and they want me to sign an NDA and I was like not signing an NDA so they give me a big back to says NDA on it that I have to wear around the campus.
segments.zh: 我到了门洛帕克，他们想让我签保密协议，我说不签，于是他们给了我一个背后写着NDA的大牌子，我必须戴着它在园区里走动。

segments.en: But because I didn't sign that NDA I'm actually tell real stories about what happened and one of the things I learned was the difference between being in a dialogue and negotiating.
segments.zh: 但因为我没有签那份保密协议，我才能讲述真实发生的故事。我学到的一件事是“对话”和“谈判”之间的区别。

segments.en: Your opponents want to keep you in a dialogue. They want to say we're talking to that group. We've heard those clive and activists.
segments.zh: 你的对手想让你停留在对话中。他们想说：我们正在和那个团体谈，我们听到了那些活动人士的声音。

segments.en: We've heard the women that are upset about this and we're listening to them and we're really concerned.
segments.zh: 我们听到了对此不满的女性，我们在倾听，我们真的很关心。

segments.en: When you have it when you're in negotiation you have leverage. You have the ability to actually move something but knowing the difference between whether just in a conversation that feels good and whether or not you have the ability to actually make meaningful change is the difference between presence and power.
segments.zh: 当你处于谈判中时，你有杠杆，你有能力真正推动事情。但知道是仅仅进行一场感觉良好的对话，还是拥有真正做出有意义改变的能力，这就是“在场”和“权力”的区别。

segments.en: And far too often we can be incentivized to want to be in the room. We want to be incentivized to feel like we've been shouted out or our concerns have been amplified but those are not the same as actually moving things along.
segments.zh: 很多时候，我们被激励着想要进入那个房间，想要感觉自己的声音被听到，担忧被放大，但这些并不等同于真正推动事情前进。
